caption:
China's biggest tech companies are giving their AI chatbots away for free and paying users to try them.
DeepSeek, Qwen, Doubao, ERNIE and Kimi all have free versions, and the top apps spent over $1.1 billion on holiday promotions this year, by Morgan Stanley's estimate.

Which of these would you try first?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: NPR

slides.headline: China is giving away its best AI *for free*, and paying people to use it

slides.heading: *DeepSeek* started it
paras: DeepSeek's chatbot launched in January 2025 and is free on web, Android and iOS. Within weeks it passed ChatGPT as the top free app on the U.S. App Store.
Reuters says DeepSeek set off a price war across China's AI industry.

slides.heading: Alibaba's *Qwen*
paras: Alibaba relaunched its consumer chatbot as Qwen, a free app and website it calls "the best personal AI assistant with the most powerful model."
For Lunar New Year, Alibaba set aside 3 billion yuan, about $431 million, in rewards to pull users into the app.

slides.heading: ByteDance's *Doubao*
paras: Doubao, from TikTok owner ByteDance, is China's most used AI app, with 155 million weekly users in late 2025, according to QuestMobile.
ByteDance says Doubao 2.0 Pro matches GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro on complex tasks at about one tenth of the usage cost.

slides.heading: Baidu's *ERNIE*
paras: Baidu made its ERNIE Bot chatbot free on April 1, 2025, including its Deep Search feature.
Baidu said cheaper computing costs let it drop the price. ERNIE Bot had about 430 million users at the time, according to Baidu.

slides.heading: Moonshot's *Kimi*
paras: Kimi, from Moonshot AI, is free to use with rate limits. It is known for very long context and agent tools that build websites and slides.

paras.t: In China, the AI race is now a fight for users, not just for the smartest model.

slides.hook: Free Chinese AI is coming for ChatGPT's users. Follow to see who wins the price war.
